\section[\texorpdfstring{\ur{بدتر} (badtar)}{بدتر (badtar)}]{\ur{بدتر} (badtar) — worse}

\label{lesson:UR-C377-badtar}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Urdu for approximately, then the Urdu for a limit.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ur{بدتر}}
\textbf{\ur{بدتر}} — \emph{badtar} — \textquotedblleft{}worse\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ur{دوا} \ur{لیجیے،} \ur{ورنہ} \ur{حالت} \ur{بدتر} \ur{ہو} \ur{گی۔}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{davā lījiye, varnā hālat badtar ho gī.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
Take the medicine, or you will get worse.
\end{quote}

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ur{بدتر}} (\emph{badtar}) is usually traced to Persian \emph{badtar}, \textquotedblleft{}worse\textquotedblright{}: \emph{bad}, \textquotedblleft{}bad\textquotedblright{}, with \emph{-tar}, \textquotedblleft{}more\textquotedblright{}, the ending that also makes \textbf{\ur{بہتر}}, \textquotedblleft{}better\textquotedblright{}.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for saying what happens if.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{badtar}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{badtar}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{davā lījiye, varnā hālat badtar ho gī.} — Take the medicine, or you will get worse.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Urdu for approximately, then the Urdu for a limit, then say \emph{badtar} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \ur{بدتر} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}Worse\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[\texorpdfstring{\ur{عمدہ} (umdā)}{عمدہ (umdā)}]{\ur{عمدہ} (umdā) — excellent; fine}

\label{lesson:UR-C377-umda}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Urdu for a limit, then the Urdu for worse.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ur{عمدہ}}
\textbf{\ur{عمدہ}} — \emph{umdā} — \textquotedblleft{}excellent; fine\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ur{اگر} \ur{کھانا} \ur{عمدہ} \ur{ہوا} \ur{تو} \ur{ہم} \ur{پھر} \ur{آئیں} \ur{گے۔}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{agar khānā umdā huā to ham phir āeṅ ge.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
If the food is excellent, we will come again.
\end{quote}

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ur{عمدہ}} (\emph{umdā}) is usually traced, through Persian, to Arabic \emph{ʿumda}, \textquotedblleft{}a support; the best part\textquotedblright{}.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for saying what happens if.

\section[\texorpdfstring{\ur{عام} (ām)}{عام (ām)}]{\ur{عام} (ām) — common; ordinary}

\label{lesson:UR-C377-am}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Urdu for worse, then the Urdu for excellent.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ur{عام}}
\textbf{\ur{عام}} — \emph{ām} — \textquotedblleft{}common; ordinary\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ur{اگر} \ur{یہ} \ur{بیماری} \ur{عام} \ur{ہے} \ur{تو} \ur{دوا} \ur{بھی} \ur{ملے} \ur{گی۔}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{agar yih bīmārī ām hai to davā bhī mile gī.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
If this illness is common, the medicine will be easy to find.
\end{quote}

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ur{عام}} (\emph{ām}) is usually traced, through Persian, to Arabic \emph{ʿāmm}, \textquotedblleft{}general, common to all\textquotedblright{}.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for saying what happens if.

\section[\texorpdfstring{\ur{بگڑنا} (bigaṛnā)}{بگڑنا (bigaṛnā)}]{\ur{بگڑنا} (bigaṛnā) — to get worse; to go wrong}

\label{lesson:UR-C377-bigarna-worsen}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Urdu for excellent, then the Urdu for common.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ur{بگڑنا}}
\textbf{\ur{بگڑنا}} — \emph{bigaṛnā} — \textquotedblleft{}to get worse; to go wrong\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ur{اگر} \ur{موسم} \ur{بگڑا} \ur{تو} \ur{ہم} \ur{نہیں} \ur{جائیں} \ur{گے۔}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{agar mausam bigṛā to ham nahīṅ jāeṅ ge.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
If the weather turns bad, we will not go.
\end{quote}

Past (it …): \ur{وہ} \ur{کام} \ur{بگڑ} \ur{گیا}, \emph{voh kām bigaṛ gayā}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ur{بگڑنا}} (\emph{bigaṛnā}) is inherited: CDIAL lists the Hindi cousin \emph{bigaṛnā}, \textquotedblleft{}to be spoilt\textquotedblright{}, under Sanskrit \emph{vighaṭate}, \textquotedblleft{}breaks apart\textquotedblright{} (CDIAL 11673); \textbf{\ur{بگاڑنا}}, \textquotedblleft{}to spoil\textquotedblright{}, is its partner.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for saying what happens if.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright

  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{bigaṛnā}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{agar mausam bigṛā to ham nahīṅ jāeṅ ge.} — If the weather turns bad, we will not go.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Urdu for excellent, then the Urdu for common, then say \emph{bigaṛnā} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \ur{بگڑنا} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}To get worse; to go wrong\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.

\section[\texorpdfstring{\ur{سدھرنا} (sudharnā)}{سدھرنا (sudharnā)}]{\ur{سدھرنا} (sudharnā) — to get better; to mend one's ways}

\label{lesson:UR-C377-sudharna-improve}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Urdu for common, then the Urdu for to get worse.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ur{سدھرنا}}
\textbf{\ur{سدھرنا}} — \emph{sudharnā} — \textquotedblleft{}to get better; to mend one's ways\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ur{اگر} \ur{تم} \ur{سدھرے} \ur{نہیں} \ur{تو} \ur{مصیبت} \ur{میں} \ur{پڑو} \ur{گے۔}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{agar tum sudhre nahīṅ to musībat meṅ paṛo ge.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
If you do not mend your ways, you will land in trouble.
\end{quote}

Past (he …): \ur{وہ} \ur{لڑکا} \ur{سدھر} \ur{گیا}, \emph{voh laṛkā sudhar gayā}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ur{سدھرنا}} (\emph{sudharnā}) is inherited: CDIAL lists the Hindi cousin \emph{sudharnā}, \textquotedblleft{}to be mended\textquotedblright{}, under \emph{*śuddhakāra}, a form it reconstructs (CDIAL 12521); \textbf{\ur{سدھارنا}}, \textquotedblleft{}to put right\textquotedblright{}, is its partner.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for saying what happens if.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{sudharnā}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{sudharnā}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{agar tum sudhre nahīṅ to musībat meṅ paṛo ge.} — If you do not mend your ways, you will land in trouble.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Urdu for common, then the Urdu for to get worse, then say \emph{sudharnā} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
